findings.reason: the plan should either express `structured_section_spans` over `plan_headings`'s output or state in §17 why the existing public reader must stay independent, since "one public reader" is the section's own stated goal.
findings.text: §17 adds `plan_headings` as a public reader over `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` while `structured_section_spans` (already public at `reckon/_plan_html.py:94`, consumed by `reckon/_store.py`) remains a second public span producer over the same parser, and the design never says why that existing reader cannot be extended or re-expressed as a projection of the new one

findings.reason: the shared predicate's interface must be widened (return the value, or add the section-valued companion the view needs) so the marker keeps one owner, or §17's stated one-owner done-when is unsatisfiable.
findings.text: §17 makes one public predicate answer "whether an element is machinery" from the presence of any `data-reckon` attribute, but `_inside_structured_region` (and its callers at `mcp_views.py:2075` and `:2101`) must additionally test the attribute's *value* `"section"` to exclude a section wrapper, which re-spells the `data-reckon` literal the §17 done-when (`grep -rn '"data-reckon"' reckon/` reports an attribute test in exactly one function) forbids

findings.reason: the rule holds a surface-adding section to name a retirement/merge or the reason none is possible; "the retired walks were private" is not that statement, so §17 (and §18, "nothing is retired") must add the sentence or reduce the added surface.
findings.text: §17 records that it adds two public definitions (`plan_headings` and the machinery predicate) and that "the retired walks were private, so the net is two", naming no public definition it retires or merges and stating no reason none can be retired, while public_definitions stands at 1477

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design hides the section-digest map, the third fingerprint form and the coverage join behind an unchanged `plan_fingerprint` signature and one module-private predicate; §16 explicitly argues why its predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the `data-reckon` marker keeps a second owner, because the MCP view's section exemption cannot be expressed over the proposed presence-only predicate without re-spelling the literal.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 and §18 each add a public definition and name only private retirements or moves, so the section states no countable retirement or merge, nor why none is possible.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the existing owner for every mechanism it touches (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser`, `structured_section_spans`, `landed_section_ids`, `_fingerprint_forms`, `section_record_id`, `implementable_sections`, `_section_key`, `normalize_section`) and each citation resolves in the code as written.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §17 adds the public `plan_headings` while keeping the existing public `structured_section_spans` over the same private parser, without naming what retires or merges.
